title: Fabricating Multi-Component Lipid Nanotube Networks Using the Gliding Kinesin Motility Assay
protocol: Weigh 24.19 g of PIPES and 0.38 g of EGTA into a 1 L glass bottle.
Add 1 mL of 1 M MgCl2 to the mixture in the glass bottle.
Adjust pH to 6.9 with KOH.
Add deionized water to bring the solution to a final volume of 500 ml.
Weigh 52 mg of GTP and suspend it in 1 mL of distilled water.
Divide 100 mM GTP solution into 20 µL aliquots and store at -20 °C.
Mix 200 μL of 5x BRB80, 10 μL of 100 mM GTP solution, 100 μL of 100% glycerol, and 600 μL of deionized water to prepare the GPEM solution.
Divide GPEM solution into 100 µL aliquots and store at -20 °C.
Reconstitute vials of lyophilized tubulin in cold (4°C) GPEM solution to a stock concentration of 5 mg/mL.
Mix 4 μL of biotinylated tubulin, 4 μL of fluorescently labeled tubulin, and 24 μL of unlabeled tubulin at a final volume of 32 mL on ice.
Divide the tubulin mixture into 2 µL aliquots and store at -80 °C until needed.
Prepare a 1% w/v solution by mixing 1 g of agarose in 100 mL of deionized water in an Erlenmeyer flask.
Heat the agarose solution for 1–2 min using a standard microwave until it is completely dissolved.
Allow the heated solution to cool to 65-75°C before use.
Pipette 300-400 μL of cooled agarose solution onto a 25 mm x 25 mm glass coverslip.
Spread the melted agarose evenly across the coverslip using another pipette tip while holding the edge with gloved fingers.
Dry the agarose-coated coverslips in a 37°C incubator for at least 2 hours until transparent.
Store the dried agarose-coated coverslips by placing them, coated surface upwards, on a clean surface.
Retrieve lipids dissolved in chloroform from a -20 °C freezer.
Place the retrieved lipids in a chemical fume hood until they reach room temperature.
Calculate the volume of lipid stock needed for each component using the provided formula.
Mix the calculated volumes of lipids together in a glass vial in the chemical fume hood.
Pipette 30 μL of the mixed lipid solution onto agarose-coated coverslips on a preheated hot plate.
Spread the lipid solution across the agarose film in a circular motion using the long edge of an 18 G needle until chloroform evaporates.
Hold the edge of the coverslip with gloved fingers during spreading.
Mix 1.92 g of sucrose with 10 mL of deionized water to prepare a 560 mM sucrose solution.
Adhere an adhesive chamber to the coverslip coated with the lipid film by gently pressing it onto the coverslip, ensuring a tight seal is formed.
Add 400 µL of 560 mM sucrose solution to the chamber.
Place the coverslip into the humidity chamber and close the lid.
Place the humidity chamber on a preheated hot plate set above the melting point of the saturated lipid component of the formulation.
Add 3 g of dry casein to a 50 mL conical centrifuge tube.
Add 30 mL of 1x BRB80 to the tube and rotate until the solution becomes viscous.
Centrifuge the tube at 15,000 x g for 30 min.
Transfer the supernatant into another 50 mL conical centrifuge tube.
Discard the pellet.
Filter the solution through a 1 µm syringe filter, collecting the solution in a 50 mL conical vial.
Filter the solution through a 0.2 µm filter, collecting the solution in a 50 mL conical vial.
Determine the protein concentration by measuring the absorbance at 280 nm using a UV-Vis spectrophotometer and quartz cuvette.
Calculate the casein concentration in mg/mL using the formula provided.
Dilute the solution to 20 mg/mL in 1x BRB80.
Divide the diluted solution into 100 µL aliquots and store at -20 °C.
Prepare glucose oxidase (2 mg/mL) stock solution by mixing 2 mg of glucose oxidase with 1 mL of 1x BRB80.
Divide the glucose oxidase stock into 100 µL aliquots and store at -20 °C.
Prepare catalase (0.8 mg/mL) stock solution by mixing 0.8 mg of catalase with 1 mL of 1x BRB80.
Divide the catalase stock into 100 µL aliquots and store at -20 °C.
Prepare 2 M glucose solution by suspending 0.3 g of D-glucose in 1 mL of deionized water.
Divide the glucose solution into 100 µL aliquots and store at -20 °C.
Prepare 100 mM DTT stock by suspending 0.015 g of DTT in 1 mL of deionized water.
Divide the DTT stock into 100 µL aliquots and store at -20 °C.
Reconstitute 0.055 g of disodium ATP in 1 mL of a 100 mM MgCl2 solution to prepare a 100 mM Mg-ATP stock.
Divide the Mg-ATP stock into 100 μL aliquots and store at -20°C.
Suspend 0.055 g of AMP-PNP in 1 mL of a 100 mM MgCl2 solution to prepare a 100 mM Mg-AMP-PNP solution.
Divide the Mg-AMP-PNP solution into 100 μL aliquots and store at -20°C.
Add 25.03 mg of Trolox to 1 mL of methanol to prepare a 100 mM Trolox solution.
Store the Trolox solution at -20°C.
Dissolve 1 mg of streptavidin in 100 μL of BRB80 to make a 1 mg/mL streptavidin solution.
Divide the streptavidin solution into 2 μL aliquots and store at -80°C.
Mix 200 µL of 5x BRB80, 20 µL of casein solution, 10 µL of MgATP solution, 10 µL of Trolox, 5 µL of paclitaxel solution with 765 µL of DI water to prepare BRB90CAT.
Store the BRB90CAT at 4°C.
Mix 192 µL of BRB80CAT, 2 µL of D-glucose solution, 2 µL of glucose oxidase solution, 2 µL of DTT solution, and 2 µL of catalase solution to prepare the motility solution.
Store the motility solution at 4°C.
Dilute 2 μL of 50 mM kinesin solution in 98 μL of BRB80CAT to prepare a 1 μM kinesin solution.
Store the kinesin solution at 4°C.
Dilute 10 µL of stabilized microtubules in 90 µL of room temperature BRB80CAT to make a 10 µg/mL microtubule solution.
Store the microtubule solution at RT.
Mix 0.1 μL of 10 mg/mL streptavidin solution with 99.9 μL of motility solution to prepare a 10 µg/mL streptavidin solution.
Store the streptavidin solution at 4°C.
Dilute 5 µL of GUV stock into 55 µL of motility solution to make a 12x GUV solution.
Store the GUV solution at 4°C.
Collect a previously prepared 2 µL aliquot of tubulin from the -80 °C freezer.
Place the tubulin aliquot into a 37 °C water bath for 30 min.
Prepare a 2 mM paclitaxel solution by adding 1.71 mg of paclitaxel in 1 mL of anhydrous DMSO, and store at -20°C.
Warm 100 µL of BRB80T to 37 °C in the water bath.
After 30 min, add 100 µL of BRB80T to the tubulin aliquot to stabilize the microtubules.
Store the stabilized microtubules at room temperature (RT).
Affix two strips of double-sided tape separated by 5 mm onto a glass slide for the flow chamber.
Place a coverslip on top of the tape and press down gently with a tweezer or pen to ensure adhesion.
Pipette 30 µL of 1 mm kinesin solution into the flow cell.
Let the kinesin solution incubate in the flow cell for 5 min.
Incubate 30 µL of 10 µg/mL microtubule solution in the flow cell using a laboratory wipe pressed gently against the opposite end to facilitate solution exchange.
Wash the flow cell 1x–3x with 1x motility solution at room temperature.
Pipette 30 µL of 10 µg/mL streptavidin solution into the flow cell using a laboratory wipe pressed gently against the opposite end of the flow channel to facilitate solution exchange.
Incubate for 10 min.
Flow 30 µL of 12x GUV solution into the flow using a laboratory wipe pressed gently against the opposite end of the flow channel to facilitate solution exchange.
Incubate for 30 min.
Add 2 µL of 100 mM AMP-PNP solution to stop motility, then seal the chamber with sealant.
Transfer the flow chamber to an inverted microscope for imaging.
Choose the appropriate filter set based on the wavelengths of the fluorescent lipids or tubulin used.
Use a 100x oil objective to focus on the surface of the coverslip.
Image the LNT networks using fluorescence microscopy.
Adjust exposure time and neutral density filters to image LNTs while minimizing overexposure of GUVs.
Take standard or tiled images of the network of interest.
Acquire images in both red and green channels.
Overlay the red and green channel images to create a composite image.
Open acquired images using an image analysis software like ImageJ.
Calibrate the scale for the microscope using the set scale feature.
Fill in the pixels to mm conversion factor based on the microscope setup.
Click OK to apply the calibration settings.
Use the Multipoint line tool to measure the length of the nanotubes starting from the parent GUV.
Hold Ctrl + M to measure the length.
Hold Ctrl + D after drawing each line to keep track of which tubes have been measured.
Open the image in ImageJ and select the Threshold feature under the Image tab.
Click Apply to apply the threshold.
Draw a rectangle of known length over the desired tube.
Measure the integrated density of the area.
Divide the density by the length (in pixels) of the LNT to obtain the thickness (in pixels).
Open the image in ImageJ.
Use the Line tool to draw a line over the desired node.
Measure the node intensity in both the Oregon Green and Texas Red channels.
Move the line to the LNT and measure the LNT intensity in both the Oregon Green and Texas Red channels.
